items.title: Henry A. "Hank" Kmen Interview, 1963-02-13
items.q: He also played bass, but primarily trumpet. And in fact he played some darn good trumpet as I remember.

ctx.x: Oh, he played with some of the bands. Some of these bands that had a semi-name in those days are completely forgotten today. It was a band named Bob Sylvester that he played with. And when I met him, he was living with Bob Sylvester because he never had collected any money from him. And the only way he could collect any money from him was to live with him and deduct the lodging from what Sylvester owed him. And that was typical of the business in those days. And I guess the best he ever did was playing the stint…
What about George Horton? Was he playing trumpet there? He played trumpet.

He also played bass, but primarily trumpet. And in fact he played some darn good trumpet as I remember. Some really good New Orleans trumpet. But it was a hard thing to get into. Johnny Beresdorf was up there playing good trumpet too. But one thing I noticed about most of the New Orleans guys, with very few exceptions, they were pining for New Orleans all the time. Longing to get back and it didn't take much to convince them that they belonged back to New Orleans. That's a trait peculiar to the city. The people…
